MMM.rationale: MMM's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 reported EPS of $1.23 (GAAP) versus $2.04 a year ago, a -39.7% YoY decline, with net income down -41.3% and operating cash flow collapsing -826.6% YoY. Revenue grew a meager +1.3% YoY while gross profit declined -0.8%. The balance sheet shows total equity shrinking to $3.31B from $4.52B a year prior, with total liabilities of $32.12B against total assets of $35.44B, implying a highly leveraged position. The P/E has expanded to 27.9x from ~17-18x a year ago, placing it at the top of its 365-day range (17.3-28.3), while P/B is 23.6x near its range high (16.7-23.9). This valuation expansion has occurred alongside deteriorating earnings, making MMM expensive versus its own history. The adjusted EPS of $2.14 cited in the earnings call masks the GAAP reality of $1.23, and even the adjusted figure shows the company guiding $8.50-$8.70 for FY2026, implying H2 deceleration. Legal overhangs from PFAS and earplug litigation remain unresolved and unquantifiable. The stock has declined -6.3% over the past quarter to $146.52, yet the P/E remains elevated. No credible near-term fundamental catalyst exists to re-rate the stock higher; the Q1 earnings beat was met with selling, and management's own guidance signals H1 > H2 earnings. The combination of deteriorating GAAP profitability, balance sheet erosion, expensive valuation, and unresolved legal risk warrants a strongly negative view.
